section: Bootstrap Diagnostics of Structural Stability -- the section's CANONICAL realization
why_this_seed: Replication 68. Chosen because the Metalog fit to the ORIGINAL sample is feasible at ALL FOUR plotted orders K=4,7,10,13 and is multimodal at 7, 10 and 13 (mode counts 1/2/2/2), so every row of Figure 5 carries its highlighted bar. Under seed 200043 (replication 1, the section's canonical realization until the paper moved) the Metalog is infeasible at K=13 and QFlex-U at K=10 and 13, leaving those bars and the Persist cells blank. All four models are feasible at all four orders here. NOTE: selecting a realization on this criterion is selection on the outcome, so the paper has to say so where it uses this realization. The published Figures 4-7 and Table 4 are now this realization, not 200043.
relationship_to_canonical: This IS the canonical build. It began as a parallel build under 'Replication 68/' while reproduction/ was still pinned to replication 1; once the paper moved to replication 68 those assets were folded into reproduction/ and the parallel build was retired to not_in_paper/Replication_68_build_shell/. Its five bootstrap scripts were byte-identical to reproduction/scripts apart from SEED.
generator_note: jpse uses legacy np.random.seed + inverse-CDF. scipy.stats.johnsonsu.rvs with default_rng gives a DIFFERENT sample for the same seed.
bootstrap_scheme: rng = np.random.default_rng(200110*10_000 + b); x_boot = rng.choice(x_orig_unsorted, size=200, replace=True)
source_artifact: NONE. Seed 200043 has a stored cloud checkpoint; this realization does not, so the sorted CSV here is sort(unsorted fresh draw) exactly, with no artifact to reconcile against. bootstrap_section.verify() cannot run for this seed for that reason.

x_orig_unsorted.why: choice() selects indices, so ordering determines each replicate. The sorted artifact alone cannot reproduce the resamples.
